description:
Included templates and modules imported `with context` no longer see the variables of the block they are used in — loop variables, `{% with %}` assignments and variables assigned inside a block are all missing.

```python
from jinja2 import DictLoader, Environment

env = Environment(loader=DictLoader({
    "inc": "[{{ x }}]",
    "mod": "{% macro show() %}<{{ x }}>{% endmacro %}",
}))
print(env.from_string("{% for x in [1, 2] %}{% include 'inc' %}{% endfor %}").render())
print(env.from_string(
    "{% for x in [1, 2] %}{% import 'mod' as m with context %}{{ m.show() }}{% endfor %}"
).render())
print(env.from_string("{% with x = 'w' %}{% include 'inc' %}{% endwith %}").render())
```

```
[][]
<><>
[]
```

Expected `[1][2]`, `<1><2>` and `[w]`. Variables of the top-level context still get through — a variable assigned at the top of the template, outside any block, is visible to the include as before — and `{% from 'mod' import show with context %}` inside the loop is broken the same way as the `import`. `import ... without context` correctly sees nothing, as before.

diff --git a/tests/test_repopilot_jinja_008.py b/tests/test_repopilot_jinja_008.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..d76218d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_repopilot_jinja_008.py
@@ -0,0 +1,50 @@
+from jinja2 import DictLoader
+from jinja2 import Environment
+
+
+def make_env():
+    return Environment(
+        loader=DictLoader(
+            {
+                "inc": "[{{ x }}{{ y }}]",
+                "mod": "{% macro show() %}<{{ x }}{{ y }}>{% endmacro %}",
+            }
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def test_include_sees_loop_variables():
+    tmpl = make_env().from_string("{% for x in [1, 2] %}{% include 'inc' %}{% endfor %}")
+    assert tmpl.render() == "[1][2]"
+
+
+def test_include_sees_with_and_block_variables():
+    env = make_env()
+    assert env.from_string("{% with x = 'w' %}{% include 'inc' %}{% endwith %}").render() == "[w]"
+    assert env.from_string("{% block b %}{% set x = 'b' %}{% include 'inc' %}{% endblock %}").render() == "[b]"
+
+
+def test_import_with_context_sees_loop_variables():
+    env = make_env()
+    tmpl = env.from_string(
+        "{% for x in [1, 2] %}{% import 'mod' as m with context %}{{ m.show() }}{% endfor %}"
+    )
+    assert tmpl.render() == "<1><2>"
+    tmpl = env.from_string(
+        "{% for x in [1] %}{% import 'mod' as m without context %}{{ m.show() }}{% endfor %}"
+    )
+    assert tmpl.render() == "<>"
+
+
+def test_from_import_with_context_sees_loop_variables():
+    tmpl = make_env().from_string(
+        "{% for x in [1, 2] %}{% from 'mod' import show with context %}{{ show() }}{% endfor %}"
+    )
+    assert tmpl.render() == "<1><2>"
+
+
+def test_import_with_context_sees_with_variables():
+    tmpl = make_env().from_string(
+        "{% with x = 'w' %}{% import 'mod' as m with context %}{{ m.show() }}{% endwith %}"
+    )
+    assert tmpl.render() == "<w>"
